instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: The job involves re-rolling stainless steel foil from parent coils into retail rolls, ensuring the grade (321 or 309) matches the order and that the foil is completely free of oil or grease. Technicians wear cut gloves for safety and document the process by photographing the parent coil's mill tag and the final labeled box to prevent shipping the wrong grade.

draft.title: Stainless Steel Foil Re-rolling and Packaging
disqualifiers: Parent coil mill tag does not match the customer order grade.
releases: Retail roll is approved for shipment to Amazon customers.

steps.title: Verify Parent Coil Grade
steps.explanation: 321 and 309 foils look identical but have different temperature ratings. Mixing them up will ruin a customer's tool steel during heat treatment.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the parent coil's mill tag showing the grade (321 or 309) next to the roll.
fields.acceptance_description: The mill tag must be clearly readable and the grade must match the customer order.
fields.guidance: Ensure the grade printed on the mill tag is in sharp focus and matches the order sheet.

steps.title: Safety and Setup
steps.explanation: Foil edges are razor-sharp and will cause severe cuts if handled with bare hands.

fields.prompt: Are you wearing cut-resistant gloves for handling the foil?
fields.guidance: Cut gloves must be worn for absolutely any step that involves touching the foil.

steps.title: Re-roll and Inspect Foil
steps.explanation: Any oil or grease on the foil will bake into the customer's workpiece during heat treatment, ruining it.

fields.prompt: Did you detect any oil, grease, or residue on the foil during the run?
fields.guidance: Keep your eyes on the foil and feel it as it winds. If you see or feel any grease, that section must be scrapped immediately.

steps.title: Box and Label Verification
steps.explanation: We must prove that the grade on the retail box matches the parent coil we actually rolled.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the finished box showing the readable grade label before taping it up.
fields.acceptance_description: The retail box label must be clearly readable and match the grade verified on the parent coil mill tag.
fields.guidance: Position the box so the label is fully visible and legible in the photo.

steps.title: Sign-off
steps.explanation: The technician packing the order takes responsibility for the grade match and cleanliness of the roll.

fields.prompt: Sign to confirm the roll was inspected, boxed, and matches the order.
fields.guidance: Your signature confirms that the grade on the box matches the parent coil and no grease was present.
